NDT training in New York: how it works for New York employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for New York City and the wider state is delivered live online or onsite at your own shop, yard, plant or project site. Atlantis NDT has no New York classroom. An ASNT NDT Level III teaches Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and supports your company's examinations and certification under its own written practice. Cohort and onsite quotes arrive within one business day.

New York is a market where the paperwork is as scrutinised as the technique. A special inspection agency working for a building owner, a contractor bidding a transit or Port Authority package, a boiler repair shop, a fabricator shipping steel into a high-rise, and a utility running its own integrity programme will all ask, sooner or later, to see how your technicians were qualified. Under SNT-TC-1A the honest answer is always the same: training hours, logged experience, general, specific and practical examinations, a vision test, and certification signed by the employer against a written practice.

So when someone searches for NDT classes in New York, what they usually need is one of two things. A company needs a crew qualified to a standard that survives an audit, without losing technicians to a week of travel and without shutting down a job. An individual needs a credible route into a first employer, and a clear picture of which methods that employer uses. We build training around both situations, and we say plainly where our scope ends.

Request a New York training quote with the methods, levels and number of technicians you need.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in New York

Courses follow the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for each method, with practical exercises steered toward the product forms New York employers actually inspect: structural steel connections and fabricated members, heavy plate and pipe in power and steam systems, marine structure in the harbour, and machined components for the region's precision manufacturers.

MethodLevelsWhat New York employers use it forPrerequisite
UTI, II, IIIComplete-joint-penetration weld examination on structural steel for buildings and transit structures (AWS D1.1), thickness surveys on steam and power piping, bridge weld examinationLevel I: written-practice entry rules. Level II: Level I plus documented experience
PAUTII, IIIEncoded weld examination on heavy structural and pressure work, corrosion mapping on steam and process piping, replacing RT where the code and owner permitConventional UT Level II first
TOFDII, IIIHeavy-wall vessel and header welds for power generation and district steam, flaw height sizingUT Level II
RTI, II, IIIPipe and pressure welds in mechanical contracting and boiler repair, castings, digital radiography on componentsSeparate state radiation-safety requirements for anyone handling sources
MTI, IIFillet and partial-penetration welds on structural steel, crane and hoisting components, fatigue-prone bridge detailsWritten-practice entry rules
PTI, IIStainless and non-magnetic components, precision machined parts, weld repairs where MT is not possibleWritten-practice entry rules
VTI, IIWeld visual on every structural and pressure job, bolted connections, corrosion and coating condition surveysWritten-practice entry rules
ETI, II, IIIHeat-exchanger and condenser tubing in power plants and large building chiller plants, surface crack detection on aerospace and precision partsNone; prior UT or MT experience helps

UT for structural steel. The single biggest source of UT work around New York City is structural: complete-joint-penetration groove welds in moment frames, transfer girders and bridge members, examined to the UT clauses of AWS D1.1 (or AWS D1.5 for bridges). Our UT Level II course for New York cohorts spends real time on AWS-style angle-beam technique, indication rating and the report formats special inspection agencies expect, alongside the ASME Section V techniques used in pressure work. Candidates can check themselves with our UT Level 2 practice questions.

UT and PAUT for steam and power. Manhattan sits on one of the largest district steam systems in the United States, and the region's generating stations, steam plants and large building mechanical rooms produce steady thickness and weld examination work. PAUT courses cover focal laws, encoded scanning, setup verification and data analysis, with corrosion mapping included because a grid of spot readings often misses localised wall loss on steam lines.

RT. Radiography remains standard in boiler and pressure-vessel repair, mechanical contracting on pressure piping and many owner specifications. The course covers exposure geometry, film and digital techniques, image quality indicators and interpretation. In a city this dense, radiography also comes with serious scheduling and exclusion-zone constraints, which is one reason contractors increasingly ask for PAUT alternatives.

MT, PT and VT. These are the first certifications most New York technicians earn, and the ones every structural fabricator and erector relies on. Courses cover yoke technique, field lighting and surface preparation on steel erected at height, penetrant process control in cold weather, and weld profile gauging.

ET. Eddy current courses cover impedance-plane interpretation and probe selection, with the practical steered to tubing (large chiller and condenser bundles are common in the city) or surface-crack work for precision and aerospace parts made on Long Island and upstate.

Level III. Preparation for the ASNT Basic and Method examinations plus procedure writing, delivered live online. See ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in New York, step by step

  1. Written practice in place. Your employer adopts a written practice based on SNT-TC-1A defining training hours, experience, examinations, vision requirements and recertification for each method and level.
  2. Formal training. You complete the classroom hours the written practice requires, live online, onsite or blended. Use the training-requirements matrix for the SNT-TC-1A recommended figures; your written practice may set higher ones.
  3. Supervised experience. You log hours doing the method under a certified Level II or III. On a busy New York project this can accumulate quickly; in a quiet shop it can take far longer.
  4. General examination on method principles, equipment and terminology.
  5. Specific examination on the employer's procedures, equipment and the codes it works to (AWS D1.1 for a structural fabricator, ASME Section V and the construction code for a pressure contractor, and so on).
  6. Practical examination on real specimens with known flaws, graded by a Level III or a qualified examiner under one.
  7. Vision examination: near-vision acuity (at least annually under SNT-TC-1A) and colour-contrast differentiation at the interval the written practice sets.
  8. Certification signed by the employer's certifying authority.
  9. Recertification at the interval the written practice sets (SNT-TC-1A recommends a maximum of five years), by re-examination or documented continuing performance.

For the employer-side explanation, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for New York crews

New York's geography makes delivery a practical question. A fabricator in the Bronx, an erector working in Hudson Yards, a boiler contractor in Queens and a machine shop in Suffolk County all lose real money when a technician spends a day in transit. Our options:

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory in real time for Level I and II and Level III preparation, scheduled around shift patterns, including evening sessions where needed. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite. An ASNT Level III-led team runs the course and practical examinations at your shop or facility, on your equipment and on specimens that resemble your work. See corporate NDT training.
  • Blended. Online theory followed by a concentrated onsite practical and examination block, which suits contractors who cannot pull a crew off active projects.

We plan around New York's own calendar: building-construction schedules that run year-round, planned outages at power and steam plants that tend to fall in the spring and autumn shoulder seasons when demand is lowest, and the winter weather that makes field MT and PT harder. If a project start date or client audit is fixed, we work backward from it. Ask about onsite training for your New York crew.

Practical examinations are always hands-on, on real specimens. We do not run remote practicals.

Where NDT technicians work in New York

Bridges, tunnels, transit and the city's special inspection regime are covered elsewhere on this page. Here is the rest of the picture that shapes which methods and credentials local employers ask for.

Structural steel fabrication and erection. Fabricators in the five boroughs, Long Island, the Hudson Valley and across the river in New Jersey supply steel for towers, hospitals, transit structures and airport projects such as the JFK terminal redevelopment. The inspection code is AWS D1.1 for buildings and AWS D1.5 for bridges, and NDT on those projects is often performed by technicians working for special inspection agencies or fabricators' in-house QC. Many of those employers also ask for AWS CWI for weld inspectors; that is a separate scheme we do not train.

Major transportation construction. Beyond the transit capital programme, the Gateway Hudson Tunnel Project and ongoing airport and bridge rehabilitation keep demand steady for UT, MT and VT on structural steel and for specialised assessments on concrete structures.

Power, steam and utilities. In-city generating stations, the district steam system and the gas and electric utilities need thickness surveys, weld examination on repairs and tube inspection. Pressure work follows ASME Section I, Section VIII and B31.1, with repairs under the National Board Inspection Code. Upstate, New York's nuclear plants near Oswego and Rochester run outages under ASME Section XI, where nuclear UT typically requires performance demonstration qualification on top of SNT-TC-1A training.

Manufacturing and aerospace supply. Long Island has a long aerospace and defence supply base, and upstate New York builds turbines and heavy machinery. Aerospace primes often require NAS 410 qualification from their suppliers, which is a different scheme; industrial manufacturers commonly accept SNT-TC-1A.

Harbour and offshore wind. Ship repair, barge fabrication and the offshore wind staging at the South Brooklyn Marine Terminal bring MT, UT and VT on marine structure, often with classification society (ABS or DNV) requirements on the acceptance side.

Refining and terminals across the harbour. New Jersey's refinery and terminal cluster along the Arthur Kill employs technicians who live in New York, bringing API 510, 570 and 653-driven inspection work. Owners there often ask for API individual certifications for inspectors; the NDT itself is done by method-certified technicians.

Radiography licensing in New York. New York is an NRC Agreement State. Statewide, the New York State Department of Health licenses radioactive material, including sealed sources used in industrial radiography, under 12 NYCRR Part 38; the former Department of Labor program was merged into DOH in 2006. Within the five boroughs, the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene's Office of Radiological Health also regulates radioactive materials and radiation equipment. Your radiation safety officer should confirm which agency's licence, reciprocity and notification rules apply to each job, and what radiographer certification the licence requires. None of that is part of SNT-TC-1A RT certification, which covers technique and interpretation; a New York radiographer usually needs both.

What employers ask for. A current method certification and the written practice behind it, training and experience records, a current vision record, site safety training (in New York City, site safety training cards for construction sites), TWIC for port facilities, and for radiography the state or city radiation credentials. For earnings, we point to public sources in our NDT salary guide rather than quoting local figures.

Level III services and written practices for New York NDT companies

Special inspection agencies, fabricators and small NDT contractors in New York are audited from several directions: owners' QA teams, city agencies, prime contractors and ISO 9001 registrars. The most common weak point is not technician skill but the written practice and examination records behind the certifications. We help with:

  • Written practice development and review so the document matches the methods you perform and the codes your clients cite. See written practice development.
  • Examination administration: general, specific and practical examinations prepared and graded under ASNT Level III oversight, with records organised for audit.
  • Procedure writing aligned to AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5, ASME Section V or client specifications, reviewed and approved by a Level III.
  • Bid support: getting the personnel-qualification section of a prequalification package complete and consistent.

Background on the framework is on our SNT-TC-1A guidance page. Book a Level III consultation before your next audit or bid.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. New York structural and fabrication trainees usually get most value from the welding workshop; aerospace-supply trainees from the hangar. Use it to rehearse setups, scan coverage and interpretation decisions between classes. It is practice only and does not replace hands-on training, logged experience or the practical examination on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who sets course content, oversees examinations and reviews written practices and procedures for employer clients.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in New York

How do I get NDT certified in New York?

Work for, or be sponsored by, an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice; complete the training hours; log supervised experience; pass the general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test; and your employer certifies you. We provide training, exam preparation and Level III support, online or at your employer's site.

Can I take NDT training online in New York State?

Yes, for the theory portion. Live online classes are available anywhere in the state, from the city to Buffalo. Practical training and the practical examination must be hands-on.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It is set by your employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training and experience hours for UT Level I and II, and experience is usually the limiting factor. See the training-requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in New York?

The company needs a radioactive materials licence (or equipment registration) from the relevant state or city agency, and radiographers must meet that licence's certification and training requirements. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification. Confirm details with the New York State Department of Health or, inside the city, the NYC Office of Radiological Health.

What does NDT training cost in New York?

We do not publish prices. Cost depends on the method, level, group size, online versus onsite delivery and any written-practice or examination support. Send your details and we return a quote within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by New York employers?

SNT-TC-1A-based certification is the framework most US structural, pressure and utility work references, and it is what AWS D1.1 points to for NDT personnel qualification. Recognition runs through the employer's written practice and records. Some contracts also require AWS CWI, API or NAS 410 credentials, which we do not train.

Is a CWI the same as NDT certification?

No. AWS CWI certifies a welding inspector; it does not qualify someone to perform UT, MT or RT. Many New York special inspectors hold both a CWI and SNT-TC-1A method certifications.

Which method should I learn first to work in New York construction?

VT and MT, then UT. Structural steel is the biggest employer of NDT technicians in the city, and UT on complete-joint-penetration welds is the skill that raises your value most.

Can you train our special inspection agency's technicians onsite?

Yes. We run cohorts at your office or shop, examine under your written practice and hand over audit-ready records.

Do you train for nuclear outage work upstate?

We teach the SNT-TC-1A methods used in outages, including UT and ET. Nuclear utilities add their own access requirements and, for UT, performance demonstration qualification, which is outside our scope.

Does my certification transfer to a new employer?

Not automatically. The new employer reviews your documented training and experience, examines you under its written practice and certifies you.

Do you offer Level III preparation?

Yes, live online. See Level III training and our full training catalogue.
